**My Dearest Eleanor,**

It is with a trembling hand and a heart heavy with years of silence that I write these words. The wind howls at the windows of this lonely keep, and the sea roars like a beast set loose. A storm is coming—greater than any I have seen in my forty years tending this light. I fear I may not see the morning. And if I do, I fear I may not see you again.

I have thought of you often, though I have not written. I have told myself that my silence was for your protection, that the life I led—this life—was one you were never meant to know. But now, as the sky darkens and the sea rises, I feel the weight of all that I have kept hidden.

You were born in this lighthouse, my love. I remember the day you came into the world, the way the dawn broke through the clouds, as though the sea itself had paused to witness the miracle. I was proud, then. I was a man of purpose, a guardian of the shore, and I believed I could give you all you needed. But I was wrong.

I should have been there for you. I should have held you when the world was too loud, when the storms of your childhood came as fierce as the ones that now gather on the horizon. Instead, I chose duty, and in doing so, I chose to turn my back on you.

**My Dearest Eleanor,**

It is with a trembling hand and a heart heavy with years of silence that I write this letter to you. The wind howls at the window of this lonely tower, and the sea roars like a beast awakened from its slumber. A storm is upon us, and I fear it may be the last night I spend in this world.

Five years have passed since the last time I laid eyes upon you. Five years since your voice, once so full of life and laughter, was silenced by my own stubborn pride and the weight of my grief. I have spent these years in the company of the sea and the flicker of the lamp, neither of which have ever spoken to me with the warmth of a daughter’s love.

I know you must have wondered why I never came to see you, why I never answered your letters. I told myself it was for your own good, that I was protecting you from the burden of my sorrow. But I see now that I was only protecting myself, hiding behind the stone walls of this lighthouse as if they could shield me from the truth of my own failure as a father.

I have watched the tides rise and fall, the seasons turn, and the stars burn in the sky above. I have seen ships lost to the sea, and I have stood in the dark, knowing that I could not save them. But I have never stopped hoping that one day, you would find your way back to me
